paragraphs: Iridium Communications Inc. ("we," "us," or "Iridium") is a leading provider of global voice, data, and positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) satellite services. We are the only commercial provider of communications services offering true global coverage, connecting people, organizations and assets to and from anywhere, in real time. Our low-Earth orbit (LEO), L-band network provides specialized, reliable, weather-resilient communications services to regions of the world where terrestrial wireless or wireline networks do not exist or are limited, including remote land areas, open ocean, airways, the polar regions, and regions where the telecommunications infrastructure has been affected by political conflicts or natural disasters. In addition, our satellites have additional payloads to host specific additional services for other customers like Aireon LLC. We also utilize our long history operating a commercial LEO satellite system to provide a growing array of engineering and operational services to government customers and government network operators such as the U.S. Space Force.

Our primary business is to provide voice and data communications services to businesses, U.S. and foreign governments, non-governmental organizations, and consumers via our satellite network, which has an architecture of 66 operational satellites with in-orbit spares and related ground infrastructure. We utilize an interlinked mesh architecture in space to route traffic across our satellite constellation using radio frequency crosslinks between satellites. This architecture minimizes the need for local ground facilities to support the constellation, which facilitates the global reach of our services and allows us to offer services in countries and regions where we have no physical presence.

We primarily sell our products and services to commercial end users by recruiting and expanding a global wholesale distribution network, currently encompassing approximately 120 service providers, approximately 310 value-added resellers (VARs), and approximately 90 value-added manufacturers (VAMs), which create and sell technology that uses the Iridium network either directly to the end user or indirectly through other service providers, VARs or dealers. These distributors often integrate our products and services with other complementary hardware and software and have developed a broad suite of applications using our products and services to target specific industries or business areas. We expect that demand for our services will increase as more applications are developed and deployed that utilize our technology.

Our commercial business, which we view as our primary source of long-term growth, is diverse and serves markets such as emergency services, maritime, aviation, government, utilities, oil and gas, mining, recreation, forestry, heavy equipment, construction, railways and other transportation. Many of our end users view our products and services as critical to their daily operations and integral to their communications and business infrastructure. For example, multinational corporations in various sectors use our services for business telephony, email and data transfer, including telematics and personal location tracking, and to provide mobile communications services for employees in areas inadequately served by other telecommunications networks. Commercial enterprises use our services to track and control assets in remote areas and provide telematics information such as location and engine diagnostics. IoT (Internet of Things) VARs integrate our products and services into diverse solutions including asset tracking, environmental monitoring, condition-based monitoring and security and alerting solutions, which are used across industries. Ship crews and passengers use our services for ship-to-shore calling, as well as to send and receive email and data files, and to receive electronic media, weather reports, emergency bulletins, and electronic charts. Shipping operators use our services to manage operations on board ships and to transmit data, such as course, speed, fuel, weather, and other navigation service data, as well as for emergency services, as one of only two networks currently approved to provide Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) services. Increasingly, ships utilize Iridium terminals with integrated data and safety capabilities to complement and backup higher speed broadband services from other satellite operators that are subject to service outages, interference during rain, and geographic regulatory restrictions. Aviation end users use our services for air-to-ground telephony and data communications for position reporting, flight following, emergency tracking, weather information, electronic flight bag updates, and airline operational communications. Recreational users rely on our services as a safety and critical personal communications lifeline to remain in contact with friends and family, as well as for emergency distress signals.

We have also seen growing adoption of our services to support autonomous systems, for which Iridium is used for command and control, image transmission and environmental data gathering via unmanned aerial, underwater and surface vehicles. Iridium Certus® provides a platform for our partners to develop specialized broadband and midband (a term we use to describe services between our legacy 2.4 Kbps narrowband and our 128 Kbps and higher speed broadband offerings) applications on our network. In 2024, we introduced additional Iridium Certus offerings featuring Iridium Messaging Transport® (IMT®) that enable IoT applications to send more data, with greater security and natively delivered via cloud infrastructure. Throughout 2025, our VAM and VAR partners continued to innovate around our Certus IoT technology platform, developing and certifying new products and applications across industrial IoT, machine-to-machine and remote personnel use cases. With broadband

services provided for the maritime, land-mobile and aviation industries and a midband service designed for maximum mobility, Iridium Certus offers flexibility to scale device speeds, sizes, and power requirements both up and down based on the needs of the end-user. We expect that these and future Iridium Certus service offerings will continue to drive growth opportunities in our commercial business.

We are developing a new service called Iridium NTN DirectSM, which we expect to commercially launch from our existing satellite constellation in 2026. Iridium NTN Direct is a 3GPP (3rd Generation Partnership Project) standards-based service that will provide Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) and direct-to-device (D2D) connectivity across the globe when fully deployed. 3GPP is an international collaboration that develops and maintains technical specifications for mobile communications technologies, enabling global interoperability of mobile networks and devices. Iridium frequencies and technology were accepted as part of 3GPP Release 19, which allows Iridium NTN Direct to be accessible via cellular chipsets designed to 3GPP standards.

In 2024, we acquired Satelles, Inc. (Satelles), a provider of highly secure, satellite-based PNT services that complement and protect Global Positioning System (GPS) and other Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) reliant systems. Time synchronization and location data play an important role in the global economy, particularly for major industries supported by critical infrastructure, such as financial services, telecommunications, cybersecurity, shipping, and transportation. In 2026, we are introducing an Application Specific Integrated Chip (ASIC) to allow partners to more cost effectively integrate our PNT services into their diverse applications using less power and space. We believe the acquisition of Satelles and our growing portfolio of PNT applications and distribution partnerships could generate substantial growth in our service revenue, as well as incremental growth in our equipment and engineering services revenue over the coming years, from both government and commercial customers. We also believe that Iridium PNT technology and services have application and business potential in other industries, like cybersecurity identity management by providing a trusted, authenticated location for data and financial transactions.

The U.S. government, directly and indirectly, has been and continues to be our largest single customer, generating $257.0 million in revenue, representing 29% of our total revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2025. This does not include revenue from the sale of equipment that may ultimately be purchased by U.S. or non-U.S. government agencies through third-party distributors, or airtime services purchased by U.S. or non-U.S. government agencies that are provided through our commercial gateway, as we lack specific visibility into these activities and the related revenue. We operate primarily under a multi-year, fixed-price contract with the U.S. government, which we refer to as our Enhanced Mobile Satellite Services (EMSS) contract to provide specified satellite airtime services for an unlimited number of U.S. Department of War (DoW) (previously referred to as the Department of Defense) and other federal government subscribers. At signing in September 2019, the EMSS contract had a total value of $738.5 million over its seven-year term ending in September 2026. The current fixed-price annual rate of the EMSS contract is $110.5 million through September 2026, with one six-month extension option, exercisable at the election of the U.S. government, at the end of that period. We provide other services, such as Iridium Certus and Iridium PNT, to the U.S. government under separate arrangements for an additional fee.

The U.S. government owns and operates a dedicated gateway that is only compatible with our satellite network, and for which we provide certain maintenance services, and technology development engineering and support services, under contracts managed by the U.S. Space Force. The U.S. armed services, State Department, Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Customs and Border Protection, and other U.S. government agencies, as well as other nations' governmental agencies, use our voice and data services for a wide variety of applications. Our voice and data products are used for numerous primary and backup communications solutions, including logistical, administrative, morale and welfare, tactical, and emergency communications. In addition, our products are installed in ground vehicles, ships, and rotary- and fixed-wing aircraft and are used for command-and-control and situational awareness purposes. Our satellite network provides increased network security to the U.S. government because traffic is routed across our satellite constellation before being brought down to earth through the dedicated, secure U.S. government gateway. The U.S. government has made, and continues to make, significant investments to maintain and upgrade its dedicated gateway, to purchase our voice and data devices, and to invest directly and indirectly in research and development and implementation support for additional services on our network, such as Distributed Tactical Communications Services (DTCS), Iridium Managed Access-Distributed Tactical Communication System NEXT (MA-DNX) and Iridium Certus.

We also provide engineering and support services to the U.S. government under a contract awarded by the Space Development Agency (SDA) in May 2022 to General Dynamics Mission Systems, with Iridium as a subcontractor, which we refer to as the SDA contract. Under this contract, General Dynamics Mission Systems and Iridium are building ground entry points and operations centers for the DoW's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA) and will provide network operations and systems integration services for the SDA's next tranche of proliferated low-Earth orbit satellites.

At December 31, 2025, we had approximately 2,537,000 billable subscribers worldwide, representing a 3% increase compared to December 31, 2024. Total revenue increased from $830.7 million in 2024 to $871.7 million in 2025, representing a 5% increase.

We compete primarily in the mobile satellite services sector of the global communications industry. Mobile satellite services operators provide voice and data services to people and machines using a network of satellites and ground facilities, and utilize licensed radio frequency spectrum in what is called the L- or S-bands that are ideal for (among other things) consumer devices, small antennas, and battery powered devices. Satellite based L- and S-band frequencies were fully allocated by the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) in the early 1990s and are utilized by a limited number of mobile satellite operators like Iridium. Mobile satellite services are intended to meet users' needs for connectivity in all locations where terrestrial wireless and wireline communications networks do not exist, do not provide sufficient coverage, or are impaired, including rural and developing areas that lack adequate wireless or wireline networks, airways, ocean and polar regions where few alternatives exist, and regions where the telecommunications infrastructure has been affected by political conflicts or natural disasters.

Government organizations, including military and disaster response agencies, non-governmental organizations, and industrial operations and support teams depend on mobile and fixed voice and data satellite communications services on a regular basis. Businesses with global operations require reliable communications services when operating in remote locations around the world. Mobile satellite services users span many sectors, including emergency services, maritime, aviation, government, utilities, oil and gas, mining, recreation, forestry, heavy equipment, construction, railways and other transportation, among others. Many of our customers view satellite communications services as critical to their daily operations.

headings: Risks related to our satellites and network
Our satellites may experience operational problems, which could affect our ability to provide an acceptable level of service to our customers.
If our ground operations were to be disrupted, we may experience interruptions in our ability to provide service to our customers.
Our customized hardware and software may be difficult and expensive to service, upgrade or replace.
Ongoing and significant technological changes in the satellite communications industry may impair our competitive position and require us to make significant additional capital expenditures.
Cyberattacks and other security threats and disruptions could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Our satellites may collide with space debris or another spacecraft, which could adversely affect the performance of our constellation.
The space debris created by the February 2009 satellite collision may cause damage to other spacecraft positioned in a similar orbital altitude.
Risks related to our business operations
Our business plan depends on increased demand for mobile satellite services, among other factors.
Our agreements with U.S. government customers, particularly the DoW, which represent a significant portion of our revenue, are subject to termination and renewal.
Aireon, our primary hosted payload customer, may not successfully grow its business, which could reduce or eliminate the value of our agreements with, and ownership interest in, Aireon.
Our ability to protect our proprietary technology is subject to limitations.
We depend on intellectual property licensed from third parties to operate our constellation and sell our devices and for the enhancement of our existing devices and services.

Our failure to effectively manage the expansion of our portfolio of products and services could impede our ability to execute our business plan, and we may experience increased costs or disruption in our operations.
We depend on third parties to market and sell our products and services, and their inability to do so effectively could impair our revenue and our reputation.
Conducting and expanding our operations outside the United States creates numerous risks, which may harm our operations and compromise our ability to expand our international operations.
Pursuing strategic transactions may cause us to incur additional risks.
Spectrum values historically have been volatile, which could cause the value of our business to fluctuate.
We may be negatively affected by global economic conditions.
Our ability to operate our company effectively could be impaired if we lose members of our senior management team or key technical personnel.
Risks related to our capital structure and ownership of our common stock
We have a considerable amount of debt, which may limit our ability to fulfill our obligations and/or to obtain additional financing.
Our Term Loan and the credit agreement governing our Term Loan may limit our financial and operating flexibility.
Our Board of Directors may reduce, suspend or terminate our planned dividends.
Adverse changes in our credit ratings or withdrawal of the ratings assigned to our debt securities by rating agencies may negatively affect us.
The market price of our common stock may be volatile and the value of our common stock may decline.
Risks related to legal and regulatory matters
Our business is subject to extensive government regulation, which mandates how we may operate our business and may increase our cost of providing services and slow our expansion into new markets.
Interference with our satellite spectrum, including by operators seeking to repurpose L-band for terrestrial services, could adversely impact our ability to provide our services.
paragraphs: From time to time, we experience temporary intermittent losses of signal cutting off calls in progress, preventing the completion of calls when made, or disrupting the transmission of data. If the magnitude or frequency of such problems increases and we are no longer able to provide a commercially acceptable level of service, our business and financial results and our reputation would be hurt, and our ability to pursue our business plan would be compromised.

In the future, we may seek to make changes to our constellation to offer new services or adjust the power. Any such changes may require prior FCC approval, and the FCC may subject the approval to other conditions that could be unfavorable to our business. In addition, from time to time we may reposition our satellites within the constellation in order to optimize our service, which could result in degraded service during the repositioning period. Although we have some ability to remedy some types of problems affecting the performance of our satellites remotely from the ground, the physical repair of our satellites in space is not feasible.

Our products could fail to perform or could perform at reduced levels of service because of technological malfunctions or deficiencies, regulatory compliance issues, or events outside of our control, which would seriously harm our business and reputation.

Our products and services are subject to the risks inherent in a large-scale, complex telecommunications system employing advanced technology and heavily regulated by, among others, the FCC and similar authorities internationally. Any disruption to our satellites, services, information systems or telecommunications infrastructure, or regulatory compliance issues, could result in the inability or reduced ability of our customers to receive our services for an indeterminate period of time. These customers include government agencies conducting mission-critical work throughout the world, as well as consumers and businesses located in remote areas of the world and operating under harsh environmental conditions where traditional telecommunications services may not be readily available. Any disruption to our services or extended periods of reduced levels of service could cause us to lose customers or revenue, result in delays or cancellations of future implementations of our products and services, result in failure to attract customers, or result in litigation, customer service or repair work that would involve substantial costs and distract management from operating our business. The failure of any of the diverse elements of our system, including our satellites, our commercial gateway, our satellite teleport network facilities or our satellite network operations center, to function as required could render our system unable to perform at the quality and capacity levels required for success. Any system failures, repeated product failures or shortened product life, or extended reduced levels of service could reduce our sales, increase costs, or result in warranty or liability claims or litigation, cause us to extend our warranty period, and seriously harm our business.

Our satellites have a limited life and may fail prematurely, which could cause our network to be compromised and materially and adversely affect our business, prospects and profitability, or cause us to incur additional expense to launch replacement satellites.

We have in the past and may in the future experience in-orbit malfunctions of our satellites, which could adversely affect the reliability of their service or result in total failure of the satellite. In-orbit failure of a satellite or temporary outage of a service or a satellite may result from various causes, including component failure, software issues, loss of power or fuel, inability to control positioning of the satellite, solar or other astronomical events, including solar radiation and flares, and space debris. Other factors that could affect the useful lives of our satellites include the quality of construction, gradual degradation of solar panels and the durability of components. We do not have, and do not have plans to obtain, in-orbit insurance to protect against losses. As a result, a failure of one or more of our satellites, the occurrence of equipment failures and other related problems would constitute an uninsured loss. Although we do not incur any direct cash costs related to the failure of a single satellite, if a satellite fails, we record an impairment charge in our statement of operations to reduce the remaining net book value of that satellite to zero, and any such impairment charges could reduce our net income for the period in which the failure occurs. Further, a large number of such failures could shorten the expected life of our constellation, which would increase our depreciation expense, or require us to replace our constellation sooner than currently planned, which would increase our projected capital expenditures.

paragraphs: Iridium Communications Inc. ("we," "us," or "Iridium") 為全球語音、資料及定位、導航與時序 (PNT) 衛星服務的主要供應商。我們為唯一提供真正全球覆蓋的商業通訊服務供應商，可將人、組織與資產從任何地方即時連接。我們的低地軌道 (LEO)、L 帶網路提供專門化、可靠且天氣抗擾的通訊服務，服務於缺乏地面無線或有線網路的地區，包括遠離陸地、開闊海域、空域、極地地區，以及因政治衝突或天然災害而影響電信基礎設施的地區。此外，我們的衛星還具備額外載荷，可為其他客戶如 Aireon LLC 提供特定額外服務。我們也利用長久運作商業 LEO 衛星系統的經驗，為政府客戶及政府網路運營商如美國太空軍提供日益增多的工程與運營服務。
我們的主要業務是透過衛星網路，為企業、美國與外國政府、非政府組織及消費者提供語音與資料通訊服務，該衛星網路架構為 66 項運作衛星與軌道備用衛星及相關地面基礎設施。我們在軌道空間使用互聯網格架構來路由流量，透過衛星間的無線電頻率交叉鏈路進行。此架構可減少對本地地面設施的依賴，有助於我們服務的全球覆蓋，並允許我們在沒有實際據點的國家與地區提供服務。

我們主要透過招募與擴展全球 Wholesale 分銷網路來銷售產品與服務，目前包含約 120 家服務供應商、約 310 家增值經銷商 (VARs) 及約 90 家增值製造商 (VAMs)，這些經銷商創造並銷售使用 Iridium 網路的技術，直接或間接透過其他服務供應商、VARs 或經銷商對終端用戶進行銷售。這些經銷商經常將我們的產品與服務與其他補充性硬體與軟體整合，並已開發出廣泛的應用程式，以針對特定產業或業務領域。我們預期隨著更多應用程式開發與部署而使用我們的技術，對我們的服務需求將會增加。

我們的商業業務，我們視為長期成長的主要來源，是多樣化的，服務市場包括緊急服務、海運、航空、政府、電力、石油與天然氣、採礦、休閒、造林、重型機械、建設、鐵路及其他運輸。許多終端用戶將我們的產品與服務視為日常運作的關鍵，並與其通訊與業務基礎設施緊密結合。例如，各產業的跨國企業使用我們的服務進行業務電話、電子郵件與資料傳輸，包括遠端通訊與個人定位追蹤，並為在其他電信網路服務不足地區的員工提供行動通訊服務。商業企業使用我們的服務來追蹤與控制遠端資產，並提供遠端通訊資訊如位置與引擎診斷。IoT (Internet of Things) VARs 將我們的產品與服務整合至多樣解決方案中，包括資產追蹤、環境監測、條件監測與安全與警報解決方案，這些解決方案被廣泛應用於各產業。船員與乘客使用我們的服務進行船對岸通話，以及發送與接收電子郵件與資料檔，並接收電子媒體、天氣報告、緊急通報與電子海圖。運輸業者使用我們的服務來管理船上的運作，並傳送資料，如航向、速度、燃料、天氣與其他導航服務資料，以及緊急服務，作為目前僅有兩家批准提供全球海上遇險與安全系統 (GMDSS) 服務的網路之一。越來越多船舶使用整合資料與安全功能的 Iridium 終端機，以補充與備用其他衛星運營商的高速寬頻服務，這些服務可能因服務中斷、雨天干擾與地理規範限制而受影響。航空終端用戶使用我們的服務進行空對地電話與資料通訊，用於位置報告、飛行跟進、緊急追蹤、天氣資訊、電子飛機資料袋更新與航空運營通訊。休閒用戶依賴我們的服務作為安全與個人通訊的關鍵生命線，以保持與親友聯繫，以及發送緊急求救訊號。

我們也觀察到我們的服務在支援自動化系統方面有越來越多的採用，Iridium 用於這些系統的指令與控制、影像傳輸與環境資料收集，透過無人航空、水下與水面載具。Iridium Certus® 提供一個平台，讓我們的夥伴能在我們的網路中開發專門化的寬頻與中頻 (我們用此詞描述介於我們傳統 2.4 Kbps 窄頻與我們 128 Kbps 及更高速寬頻服務之間的服務) 應用程式。2024 年，我們推出了額外的 Iridium Certus 服務，包含 Iridium Messaging Transport® (IMT®)，這些服務使 IoT 應用程式能傳送更多資料，並具有更高的安全性，且原生地透過雲端基礎設施進行傳送。在 2025 年，我們的 VAM 與 VAR 合作夥伴持續創新我們的 Certus IoT 技術平台，開發並認證新的產品與應用程式，應用於工業 IoT、機器對機器與遠端人員使用案例。隨著寬頻
服務提供給海運、陸地移動與航空產業，以及一個為最大移動性設計的中頻服務，Iridium Certus 提供靈活性，根據終端用戶的需求，可向上或向下調整設備速度、尺寸與電力需求。我們預期這些及未來的 Iridium Certus 服務將持續推動我們商業業務的成長機會。

我們正在開發一個名為 Iridium NTN DirectSM 的新服務，預計在 2026 年從現有衛星星座商業發行。Iridium NTN Direct 是一個基於 3GPP (第三代合作計畫) 標準的服務，當完全部署時，將在全球提供 Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) 及直接對設備 (D2D) 連線。3GPP 是一個國際合作，開發與維護行動通訊技術的技術規格，使全球行動網路與裝置的互通性成為可能。Iridium 頻率與技術已被接受為 3GPP Release 19 的一部分，這使得 Iridium NTN Direct 可透過符合 3GPP 標準的行動晶片組進行存取。

2024 年，我們收購了 Satelles, Inc. (Satelles)，這是一家提供高度安全、基於衛星的 PNT 服務供應商，這些服務補充並保護全球定位系統 (GPS) 及其他全球導航衛星系統 (GNSS) 依賴的系統。時間同步與位置資料在全球經濟中扮演重要角色，特別是對於由關鍵基礎設施支持的主要產業，如金融服務、電信、網路安全、運輸與物流。2026 年，我們將推出應用特定整合晶片 (ASIC)，讓合作夥伴能更有效地以更低的電力與空間整合我們的 PNT 服務至其多樣應用。我們相信收購 Satelles 及我們日益增長的 PNT 應用與分銷合作夥伴，將在未來幾年為我們的服務收入帶來顯著成長，同時也為政府與商業客戶帶來設備與工程服務收入的增量成長。我們也相信 Iridium 的 PNT 技術與服務在其他產業，如網路安全身分管理方面有應用與商業潛力，透過提供一個受信任且驗證過的位置，用於資料與金融交易。

美國政府，直接或間接，一直是我們最大的單一客戶，於2025年12月31日財務年度產生257.0 百萬美元營業收入，佔我們總營業收入的29%。此數字不包含來自設備銷售的收入，這些設備最終可能由美國或非美國政府機構透過第三方經銷商購買，或美國或非美國政府機構透過我們的商業閘道購買的通話服務收入，因為我們對這些活動及相關收入缺乏具體的可見度。我們主要根據與美國政府簽訂的多年期固定價格契約運作，此契約我們稱為增強行動衛星服務（Enhanced Mobile Satellite Services, EMSS）契約，用以提供指定的衛星通話服務，供無限數量的美國國防部（Department of War, DoW）（先前稱為國防部）及其他聯邦政府訂戶使用。於2019年9月簽約時，EMSS契約總價值為738.5 百萬美元，期限為七年，至2026年9月為止。EMSS契約目前的固定價格年度金額為110.5 百萬美元，至2026年9月為止，並有一個六個月延長選項，由美國政府選擇是否行使，於該期間結束時。我們還透過其他安排，為美國政府提供其他服務，例如Iridium Certus和Iridium PNT，並收取額外費用。

美國政府擁有並運營一個專用閘道，僅與我們的衛星網路相容，我們透過由美國太空軍管理的契約，為該閘道提供某些維護服務，以及科技開發工程與支援服務。美國國防部、國務院、國土安全部、聯邦緊急管理署（FEMA）、海關與邊境保護局，以及其他美國政府機構，以及其他國家的政府機構，使用我們的語音與數據服務，用於廣泛的應用。我們的語音與數據產品用於許多主要與備用通訊解決方案，包括物流、行政、士氣與福利、戰術與緊急通訊。此外，我們的產品安裝於地面車輛、船隻、旋翼與固定翼飛機上，用於指揮與控制及情境感知用途。我們的衛星網路為美國政府提供更高的網路安全性，因為流量會先透過我們的衛星星座路由，再經由專用且安全的美國政府閘道傳輸至地面。美國政府已進行並持續進行重大投資，以維護與升級其專用閘道、購買我們的語音與數據設備，並直接或間接投資於我們網路上額外服務的研究與開發及實作支援，例如分散式戰術通訊服務（Distributed Tactical Communications Services, DTCS）、Iridium Managed Access-Distributed Tactical Communication System NEXT（MA-DNX）和Iridium Certus。

我們也根據美國太空發展局（Space Development Agency, SDA）於2022年5月授予通用動力公司（General Dynamics Mission Systems）的契約，以Iridium為分包商，我們稱為SDA契約，為美國政府提供工程與支援服務。根據此契約，通用動力公司（General Dynamics Mission Systems）與Iridium正在為美國國防部（DoW）的擴散戰鬥空間架構（Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture, PWSA）建設地面入口點與運作中心，並為SDA的下一批擴散低地軌衛星提供網路運作與系統整合服務。
於2025年12月31日，我們全球約有2,537,000個可計費訂戶，與2024年12月31日相比成長3%。總營業收入從2024年的830.7 百萬美元增至2025年的871.7 百萬美元，成長5%。

我們主要在全球通訊產業的行動衛星服務部門進行競爭。行動衛星服務運營商透過衛星與地面設施的網路，為人與機器提供語音與數據服務，並使用經許可的無線電頻率頻譜，稱為L-或S頻段，這些頻段適合（除其他用途外）消費者設備、小型天線及電池供電設備。基於國際電信聯盟（International Telecommunications Union, ITU）於1990年代初期完全分配的衛星基頻L-與S頻段，被極少數的行動衛星運營商如Iridium所使用。行動衛星服務旨在滿足用戶在無地面無線與有線通訊網路、覆蓋不足或受損的地區的連接需求，包括缺乏足夠無線或有線網路的鄉村與發展中地區、少有替代方案的空域與極地地區，以及因政治衝突或自然災害而受影響的通信基礎設施地區。
包括軍事與災難應變機構、非政府組織及工業運作與支援團隊在內的政府機構，定期依賴行動與固定語音與數據衛星通訊服務。在全球運作的企業在世界各地的偏遠地區運作時，需要可靠的通訊服務。行動衛星服務用戶來自許多產業，包括緊急服務、海運、航空、政府、電力與能源、礦業、休閒、林業、重型機械、建設、鐵路及其他運輸，等等。許多我們的客戶將衛星通訊服務視為其日常運作的關鍵。

paragraphs: 本公司為全球語音、數據及定位、導航與時脈（PNT）衛星服務的主要提供者，並為唯一提供真正全球覆蓋之通訊服務之商業服務商，可將人、機構與資產從任何地點即時連接。本公司之低地軌道、L頻段衛星網路，可為缺乏地面無線或有線網路之世界區域提供可靠、抗天氣影響之通訊服務，包括遠離陸地之區域、開闊海域、空域、極地地區及因政治衝突或自然災害而遭破壞之電信基礎設施之區域。
本公司透過衛星網路為企業、美國與外國政府、非政府組織及消費者提供語音與數據通訊服務，該衛星網路架構包含66顆運作衛星與軌道備用衛星及相關地面基礎設施。本公司利用互聯網狀架構，透過衛星間之無線電頻率交叉鏈路來路由流量。此獨特架構可減少對地面設施之需求，有助於本公司服務之全球覆蓋，並使本公司能在無實際據點之國家與地區提供服務。

2024年，本公司收購Satelles, Inc.（Satelles），一家提供高度安全、基於衛星之PNT服務之公司，其服務可補充並保護GPS及其他全球導航衛星系統依賴系統。時間同步與位置資料在全球經濟中扮演重要角色，特別是對依賴關鍵基礎設施之主要產業，如金融服務、電信、網路安全與運輸。本公司認為此收購有潛力在未來幾年為本公司服務收入帶來顯著成長，同時也從政府與商業客戶產生額外之設備與工程服務收入。
本公司透過 Wholesale 分銷網路向商業最終用戶銷售產品與服務，該網路包含約120家服務供應商、310家增值經銷商（VARs）及90家增值製造商（VAMs），這些經銷商或直接銷售給最終用戶，或透過其他服務供應商、VARs 或經銷商間接銷售。這些經銷商往往
將本公司之產品與服務與其他補充性硬體與軟體整合，並為本公司產品與服務開發廣泛之應用程式，以針對特定業務線。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司全球約有2,537,000名可計費用戶，較2024年12月31日約2,460,000名可計費用戶增加77,000名，增幅為3%。本公司擁有多元之客戶羣，包括陸地移動、物聯網（IoT）、海運、航空與政府之最終用戶。

本公司主要從提供服務與銷售設備中認列收入。服務收入於2025年12月31日止年度及2024年12月31日止年度分別佔總收入之73%與74%。語音與數據、IoT數據與寬頻服務收入歷來產生較高之毛利率，本公司預期此趨勢將持續。本公司亦從本公司之 hosted payloads 認列收入，主要來自 Aireon，包括 hosting 製品之費用及透過本公司網路傳送資料之費用，以及來自其他服務之收入，如衛星時間與位置服務。

headings: 與我們衛星及網路相關的風險
我們的衛星可能遭遇運作問題，這可能會影響我們提供給客戶可接受的服務水準的能力。
若我們的地面運作受到幹擾，我們可能會遭遇無法提供服務給客戶的中斷。
我們的客製化硬體及軟體可能難以維護、升級或更換，且成本可能高昂。
衛星通訊產業持續且重大的技術變革，可能削弱我們的競爭地位，並要求我們進行重大額外的資本支出。
網路攻擊及其他安全威脅與中斷，可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
我們的衛星可能與太空碎片或其他飛行器碰撞，這可能會對我們的星羣運作造成不利影響。
2009 年 2 月衛星碰撞所產生的太空碎片，可能對位於相似軌道高度的其他飛行器造成損害。
與我們業務運作相關的風險
我們的業務計畫依賴於行動衛星服務需求的增加，以及其他因素。
我們與美國政府客戶的協議，特別是與美國國防部（DoW）的協議，代表我們營業收入的顯著部分，這些協議可能終止或續約。
Aireon 為我們的主要載具負載客戶，若 Aireon 未能成功拓展其業務，可能會降低或消除我們與 Aireon 之間的協議價值及我們在 Aireon 中的股權利益。
我們保護專有技術的能力受到限制。
我們依賴第三方授權的智慧財產權來運作我們的衛星星座，銷售我們的設備，以及提升我們現有的設備和服務。
我們若無法有效管理我們產品與服務組合的擴張，可能會阻礙我們執行業務計畫，並可能導致我們營運成本增加或營運中斷。
我們依賴第三方來行銷與銷售我們的產品與服務，若這些第三方無法有效進行，可能會影響我們的營收與聲譽。
進行並擴展我們在美國境外的業務運作，會產生許多風險，這些風險可能影響我們的運作並削弱我們擴展國際業務的能力。
追求戰略交易可能導致我們面臨額外的風險。
Spectrum 的價值歷來波動很大，這可能會導致我們業務價值出現波動。
我們可能受到全球經濟狀況的負面影響。
如果我們失去高階管理團隊或關鍵技術人員，可能會影響我們有效運作公司的能力。
與我們資本結構及我們普通股持股相關的風險
我們擁有相當大的債務，這可能會限制我們履行義務及/或取得額外融資的能力。
我們的定期貸款及規範該貸款的信用協議可能會限制我們的財務及營運彈性。
本公司董事會可能減少、中止或終止我們預定的股息。
我們信用評級的不利變動或信用評級機構撤回對我們債務證券所給予的評級，可能會對我們產生負面影響。
我們普通股的市場價格可能波動，且我們普通股的價值可能下跌。
與法律及法規事項相關的風險
我們的業務受廣泛政府監管，這些監管要求我們如何運作業務，可能會增加我們提供服務的成本，並延緩我們進入新市場的擴張。
幹擾我們的衛星頻譜，包括由業者尋求將L頻段重新用於地面服務，可能會對我們提供服務的能力產生負面影響。
paragraphs: 偶爾，我們會遭遇暫時性間歇性訊號中斷，導致進行中的通話中斷、無法完成新通話，或幹擾資料傳輸。若此類問題的嚴重程度或發生頻率增加，且我們無法繼續提供商業上可接受的服務水準，將會對我們的業務與財務結果及聲譽造成傷害，並影響我們執行業務計畫的能力。
未來，我們可能考慮調整衛星星座以提供新服務或調整功率。任何此類變更可能需要先獲得 FCC 的批准，且 FCC 可能對批准附加其他條件，這些條件可能對我們的業務不利。此外，我們偶爾可能重新定位星座中的衛星以優化服務，這可能會在重新定位期間導致服務品質下降。雖然我們有部分能力透過地面遠端解決影響衛星性能的問題，但無法在太空中進行物理維修。
我們的產品可能因技術故障或缺陷、法規合規問題，或我們無法控制的事件而無法正常運作或運作水準降低，這將嚴重影響我們的業務與聲譽。

我們的產品與服務面臨大型、複雜的電信系統所固有的風險，該系統採用先進技術，並受到多個機構的嚴格監管，包括 FCC 及國際上類似機構。任何對我們衛星、服務、資訊系統或電信基礎設施的中斷，或法規合規問題，都可能導致我們的客戶在一段無法預測的時間內無法接收我們的服務。這些客戶包括在全球執行關鍵任務工作的政府機構，以及位於世界遠離地區、在惡劣環境下運作的消費者與企業，這些地區傳統電信服務可能不易取得。任何服務中斷或服務水準降低的時間過長，都可能導致我們失去客戶或收入，造成未來產品與服務實施計畫的延遲或取消，導致無法吸引客戶，或引發訴訟、客戶服務或維修工作，這些都可能產生重大成本並分散管理層的經營重點。我們系統中任何多樣元件，包括衛星、商業門戶、衛星電臺網路設施或衛星網路運營中心，若無法如預期運作，將使我們的系統無法達到成功所需的品質與容量水準。任何系統故障、反覆產品故障或產品壽命縮短，或服務水準降低的時間過長，都可能減少我們的銷售，增加成本，或導致保固或責任申索或訴訟，使我們延長保固期間，並嚴重影響我們的業務。
我們的衛星壽命有限，可能提前失效，這可能導致我們的網路受到損害，並對我們的業務、前景與獲利造成重大且不利的影響，或導致我們必須增加費用以發射替代衛星。

我們過去曾且未來可能遭遇衛星在軌運作時的故障，這可能影響其服務的可靠性，或導致衛星完全失效。衛星在軌運作故障或服務暫時中斷，可能由多種原因造成，包括零組件故障、軟體問題、電力或燃料喪失、無法控制衛星定位、太陽或其他天文現象，包括太陽輻射和耀斑，以及太空碎片。影響我們衛星使用壽命的其他因素包括建造品質、太陽能板逐漸退化以及元件的耐用性。我們目前沒有，也沒有計畫取得軌道保險以保護損失。因此，一顆或多顆衛星的故障、設備故障及其他相關問題將造成未投保的損失。雖然我們不會因單一衛星故障而產生直接現金成本，但若衛星故障，我們會在營運損益表中記錄減損費用，將該衛星的剩餘淨帳面價值減至零，任何此類減損費用都可能減少該期間的淨收入。此外，大量此類故障可能縮短我們星座的預期壽命，這將增加我們的折舊費用，或迫使我們比目前計畫更早更換星座，這將增加我們預期的資本支出。
